claims.statement: The base rule for practising medicine in Chile is Código Sanitario art. 112: only holders of the respective title granted by the Universidad de Chile or another State-recognised university, who are additionally legally habilitados, may perform activities proper to medicine.

claims.statement: A published, sourced rheumatology-workforce number exists only for PAEDIATRIC rheumatology: 31 paediatric rheumatologists registered with the Superintendencia de Salud, present in only 7 regions and 14 public centres, 61.3% of them in the Región Metropolitana, against an estimated need of 25 full-time clinical posts; I found NO equivalent published national count or brecha figure for ADULT rheumatology.

sources.title: Reumatología pediátrica en Chile: pasado, presente y futuro

Hay dos patologías incorporadas en el régimen GES. Se estima que se requieren 25 médicos a tiempo completo para labores exclusivamente clínicas para suplir la demanda de la población infantil hasta los 18 años.

claims.statement: At the level of the whole medical workforce there is a documented and quantified gap: MINSAL counted 24,073.25 full-time-equivalent (JCE) medical posts at December 2024 and the Plan de Inversiones en Salud 2025-2035 says a further 7,156.5 JCE, about 30% more, would be needed for the infrastructure to function properly; the shortage specialties that source names are oncology-related, intensive care, emergency medicine, geriatrics and anaesthesia, NOT rheumatology.

claims.statement: There is a real, unresolved procedural conflict on the Ley 20.985 route: the Superintendencia's specialty-inscription page requires the applicant to be already habilitada to practise in Chile, while Ley 20.261 art. 2 bis expressly contemplates certifying doctors who are NOT habilitados, and CONACEM says enforcement of that norm rests with the Superintendencia's Intendencia de Prestadores; no published page explains how such a certificate is actually recorded.

entities.name: Universidad de Santiago de Chile and Agencia de Certificación de la Universidad de Concepción (ACUDEC)

open_questions.question: Does the Superintendencia de Salud actually record a CONACEM certificate issued under Ley 20.985 to a doctor who is NOT habilitada to practise, given that its own specialty-inscription page demands prior habilitación?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If the certificate cannot be recorded in the RNPI it may be unusable for public-sector hiring and for FONASA specialist tariffs, which would destroy the value of the whole Ley 20.985 route.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Written query to the Intendencia de Prestadores citing Ley 20.261 art. 2 bis, plus a query to CONACEM asking how many Ley 20.985 certificates have been issued and registered in the last three years.

open_questions.question: Do her Ukrainian credentials evidence a separate INTERNAL MEDICINE qualification, or a single integrated programme covering internal medicine and rheumatology?
open_questions.why_it_matters: CONACEM's Reumatología rule demands prior Medicina Interna certification, but the general Formación en el Extranjero rule allows a single derived-specialty certification where the foreign programme was one integrated course of usually not less than four years. Which applies decides whether she faces two exam pairs or one.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Obtain the official Ukrainian programme document and put it to the CONACEM Comité de Reumatología in writing before paying any fee.

open_questions.question: Can any part of the CONACEM process be done from abroad, and is a mandatario with a poder notarial accepted for lodging documents and collecting the diploma?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The written and practical exams clearly require presence in Chile, but if the application itself can be lodged and decided remotely she could learn whether equivalence is accepted before spending on travel.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Ask CONACEM directly (informaciones@conacem.cl) whether the online registration and the antecedentes review can proceed with an address abroad.

open_questions.question: Is CONACEM's MINSAL authorisation for Reumatología currently in force? The Superintendencia registry page shows an authorisation dated 23-02-2017 with a stated vigencia of 5 years and no renewal row.
open_questions.why_it_matters: If the authorisation has lapsed for that specialty, a CONACEM rheumatology certificate might not be registrable.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Ask the Intendencia de Prestadores for the current Registro de Entidades Certificadoras extract for CONACEM.

open_questions.question: Does the Tribunal Constitucional case law reported to have declared the Ley 20.261 art. 2 bis 'sólo para el sector público' limitation inapplicable in individual cases create any usable route to private practice, or is it strictly inter partes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the difference between being confined to public hospitals and being able to work in a clínica privada.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Obtain the TC rulings (the 2020 inaplicabilidad reported by Diario Constitucional, whose page returned HTTP 403 to me) and a Chilean health-law opinion. Treat it as litigation, not as a procedure.

open_questions.question: Do ISAPREs pay a doctor at specialist rates when the specialty is not registered at the Superintendencia?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It determines her realistic private income in the years before certification.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Read the Superintendencia's Compendio de Normas Administrativas en Materia de Beneficios and confirm with two ISAPREs directly. I did not verify this and make no claim about it.

open_questions.question: How many adult rheumatologists are registered in the RNPI today, and is adult rheumatology on any MINSAL brecha-de-especialistas priority list?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the demand side of the whole plan, and lane L11's verdict depends on it.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Query the RNPI search at https://rnpi.superdesalud.gob.cl/ filtering by specialty, and request the MINSAL brechas dataset under the Ley de Transparencia.

open_questions.question: Will the Superintendencia accept, for RNPI inscription, a revalidación granted by a State university other than the Universidad de Chile under the post-17-August-2026 regime?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every Superintendencia page I read speaks generically of 'reconocimiento o revalidación' and was last updated in March 2026, i.e. before the change. If the RNPI back-office validation is hard-wired to the Universidad de Chile, a revalidación from USACH or Valparaíso could stall at the registry.
open_questions.how_to_resolve: Written query to the Intendencia de Prestadores. Cross-reference lanes L01 and L03.

unknowns_declared: I could not find any published national count of ADULT rheumatologists in Chile, nor any MINSAL brecha figure specific to rheumatology. The only hard, sourced rheumatology workforce number I verified is for PAEDIATRIC rheumatology (31 registered, 2023 article).
I did not verify how ISAPREs treat an uncertified specialist for billing purposes. The FONASA MLE rule is documented; the ISAPRE side is not, and I make no claim about it.

I could not retrieve the Tribunal Constitucional ruling on the 'sólo para el sector público' limitation (diarioconstitucional.cl returned HTTP 403). Its existence is reported by search results only, so I recorded it as a trap flag rather than as a claim.
I did not verify whether Universidad de Santiago de Chile or ACUDEC (Universidad de Concepción) certify Reumatología or accept Ley 20.985 applicants; only CONACEM was verified for Reumatología.

The CONACEM Reumatología requirements page carries no date at all, so under this project's rules it is treated as stale, even though the general-requirements page it depends on was updated 26-11-2025.

CONACEM publishes no total processing time. Every duration in process_steps is my estimate derived from the published exam cadence (at least twice a year), the one-month notice, the roughly one-month marking period and the 18-month completion window; they are NOT quoted from any source.
The Superintendencia publishes no processing time for RNPI inscription either; the 15-90 day range in process_steps is my estimate, not a source figure.

No fee in this lane is expressed in UTM. CONACEM fees are nominal Chilean pesos set by board resolution (last published reajuste effective 1 January 2024) and RNPI inscription is free, so there is no UTM figure to record.

I did not test whether the Superintendencia will accept a paper RNPI application from an apoderado for a person with no RUN; I established only that the ONLINE form makes RUN mandatory and offers Chilean regiones and comunas only.

Whether her Ukrainian rheumatology qualification will be judged equivalent in duration, content and depth to the Chilean programme is a discretionary decision of the CONACEM Comité, is expressly unappealable on the equivalence point, and cannot be predicted from any public source.

I did not establish whether a Ley 20.985 certified specialist can be appointed to a Servicio de Salud post under Ley 19.664 without also satisfying the Estatuto Administrativo nationality rule; that interacts with lane L06 and lane L09 and is unresolved here.
